text.p: Following are comments on the second interest rate cut in three days by Norway's Central Bank.

"I see this as an attempt to win back control over the debt market. The Central Bank has been trying to control both the foreign exchange and interest rate market and that could not last. The development we see now is a classic example of this."
"There is a cabinet meeting today and that means that foreign exchange regulations could be changed. I think that's what we must focus on now."

"It is very unfortunate to continue cutting rates given the economic phase we are in at the moment. It now loos as though they (Norwegian authorities) will permit a certain strengthening in the crown and they will permot a somewhat more flexible interpretation of currency regulations."

"If the crown is returned to a managed float again I would not be surprised if we had the same problems erupting in the future. We see strong demand for the crown. There are expectations of a current acount surplus of eight or nine percent of GDP and that implies that there is going to be strong demand for the crown.
